source: Watermelon (ដំណាំ ឪឡឹក) cultivation factsheet, undated; source publisher not stated on the visible pages but the structure and layout are consistent with MAFF/GDA vegetable-crop factsheet series (elibrary.maff.gov.kh). Uploaded PDF, no cover page present.
text:
Watermelon requires nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K) fertilizer applied in stages through the growing cycle, generally split into a base/land-preparation dose plus at least three top-dressing applications timed to the crop's development.

At land preparation, compound fertilizer 15-15-15 is applied at about 200 kg per hectare, worked into the soil.

A first top-dressing, applied about 10 days after sowing/transplanting, focuses on nitrogen-rich fertilizer (such as urea) since the young plant needs more nitrogen at this stage to support vegetative growth.

Later top-dressing applications continue to use 15-15-15 compound fertilizer at roughly 200-250 kg per hectare per application at intervals of about 20-25 days, applied by placing fertilizer beside the plant row/near the base and then covering it with soil, followed by irrigation to help it dissolve into the root zone.

A final top-dressing stage, timed around 15-25 days before an expected first harvest, emphasizes potassium (K2O), applied at about 45-50 kg per hectare, to help the fruit develop good red flesh color, sweetness, and firmness before ripening; NPK ratios and rates should be adjusted to the actual soil fertility and the variety being grown (some sources also reference triple superphosphate/DAP style products for the phosphorus component, applied similarly around 20-25 days after sowing at roughly 200-250 kg per hectare).
